title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.43): V is a real 2-dimensional vector space carrying a 'combinatorial polygon' J̃, a regular m-gon whose vertices are the vectors R̃_j (j ∈ J̃, |J̃| = m). D = Aut(V, J̃) is the dihedral group of order 2m. D^+ ≅ Z/m is its rotation subgroup, the kernel of D → Aut(orientations) ≅ Z/2. On this page m = 2n is assumed even.

(7) Because m is even, the symmetry a_0 : x ↦ −x lies in D^+, and it is the unique element of order 2 in the cyclic group D^+. The margin note records that {1, a_0} is the centre of D.

(8) For each vertex J, r_J is the unique non-identity element of D fixing R̃_J. It is the reflection in the line through R̃_J.

(9) r_J = r_{a_0(J)}, since the opposite vertex −R̃_J lies on the same line. So the vertex reflections give only n = m/2 distinct reflections. These are half of the coset D^− = D \ D^+ (m reflections in all). The other n reflections are the axes through midpoints of edges ('côtés').

Finally, there is a unique D-invariant (even D^+-invariant) quadratic form on V that equals 1 on the R̃_J. This makes V a Euclidean plane.

Purpose (next page): pass to V_C and Σ = P(V_C) ≅ P^1_C. D acts on Σ through D' = D/{1, a_0} ≅ dihedral group D_n. The images R_i satisfy R_i = R_{a_0(i)}, so they are indexed by J = J̃/{1, a_0}. This gives n points on P^1 with dihedral symmetry: the standard 'regular polygon' configuration (n-th roots of unity, with 0 and ∞) used as a base point / symmetric object in the genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid / moduli spaces M_{0,n}.
errors: Uniqueness of the invariant quadratic form (and the claim that D^+-invariance alone suffices) needs m ≥ 3, i.e. n ≥ 2. For m = 2, D^+ = {1, a_0} acts by scalars and D is a Klein four-group, so the invariant forms form a 2-dimensional space. Likewise, the centre of D is only {1, a_0} when n ≥ 2; the margin seems to note this exception ('sauf si...').
Minor: the stabilizer statement (8) is correct (the stabilizer of a vertex vector in D is {1, r_J}). Nothing else is wrong.

ideas.what: In a dihedral group of order 2m with m even, −1 is the unique involution among rotations and generates the centre.
The reflections of a regular 2n-gon split into n vertex axes and n edge axes; opposite vertices give the same reflection.
ideas.modern_name: two conjugacy classes of reflections in D_{2m}, m even

ideas.what: Unique invariant Euclidean structure normalized on the vertices; preparation for the action of D/{±1} ≅ D_n on P(V_C) with n marked points.
ideas.modern_name: dihedral symmetry of the cyclotomic point configuration in M_{0,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; its use for Teichmüller towers appears in Esquisse d'un programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses dihedral/cyclic symmetric base points of M_{0,n} in general terms

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary bookkeeping on dihedral groups and regular polygons, setting up the symmetric point configuration on P^1. It is correct (up to the trivial m = 2 exception) and contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Margin note likely reads 'NB Le centre de D est réduit à {1, a_0}, sauf si n = 1 ...' (with 'groupe' or 'avant' crossed out), not 'Le groupe D^+/D est réduit à {1,a_0}'. The next page confirms 'centre {1, a_0}'.
Line under (9): 'r_J distinctes, qui correspondent à la moitié {+aux sommets+} des éléments de la classe D^- de D modulo D^+' — the insertion is 'aux sommets', placed over the underlined 'moitié'.
Struck block near (7) at right: a deleted variant about an element of order 2; it is not part of the text.
